Look concretely for: any `q.ask` value other than 'reading' silently falling through into the `check` branch (counted:false, built from a possibly absent proposal); the final `.sort((a, b) => rank[a.ask] - rank[b.ask])`, which has no tiebreak and compares `undefined` (NaN) when an `ask` value is not in `rank`; `Number(row?.rule)` producing NaN when `block.rows.find(...)` returns no row, while `line`/`ruleText` are taken from the question instead of the row; the `check` branch stringifying/plain-words-ing `q.proposal` that may be null/undefined so `reading` and `check` disagree; `applyChoices` applying every `block.applyAnswer` against the pre-reconcile `open` list and calling `block.reconcile()` only once at the end, so a later choice whose key was invalidated by an earlier one lands in `refused`; and any place `r` from `applyAnswer` is used without checking it exists. Then write the answer file at output/steps/1.json (writing the file creates output/steps/): a complete, valid JSON object {"results": [...]} and nothing else — no "text", no "cites". Put one object per bug you found, most serious first (2 to 4 items is plenty). Each object has exactly the keys "file" (always the repo path src/blockasks.js, nothing else), "quote" (words copied verbatim from src/blockasks.js, a few lines at most, no paraphrasing, no added line-number prefixes), and "why" (plain prose that names the line number of that problem, e.g. 'line 14: ...'). Do not invent a defect you cannot quote; do not mention any file other than src/blockasks.js.

Own the whole goal: a review of src/blockasks.js that lists the bugs found and names the line number of each problem, delivered as output/steps/1.json. Re-read src/blockasks.js (read it, plus grep for each quoted snippet you used) and re-open output/steps/1.json, then repair and rewrite the file so it satisfies the goal end to end. Check and fix each of these: every item's "quote" appears word for word in src/blockasks.js (same characters, same spacing; no ellipses, no line-number prefixes, no markdown bold around it); every "why" names the specific line number of that problem and explains the defect rather than restating the quote; "file" is exactly src/blockasks.js; the top-level object is {"results": [...]} with no "text", no "cites", no extra keys and no trailing commentary; the JSON closes properly (a file cut off before its closing brace counts as not written). If a quote cannot be matched exactly, replace it with one you can match or drop that item; add an item only when you can quote it verbatim. You may edit any file under output/; never edit anything under input/ and never edit src/blockasks.js.

+      "why": "line 34: every choice is applied against the pre-reconcile `open` list and `block.reconcile()` is only called once, after the loop at line 37, so a choice whose key was only valid before an earlier choice changed things is applied against stale state and ends up in `refused` even though the person's sequence was sound; line 37: reconcile should run between choices, not only once at the end."
+    },
+    {
+      "file": "src/blockasks.js",
+      "quote": "    const row = block.rows.find((r) => r.key === q.rowKey);\n    const rule = Number(row?.rule);\n    const base = { key: q.key, rowKey: q.rowKey, line: q.line, rule, source: /** @type {'look'} */ ('look'), ruleText: String(q.ruleText) };",
+      "why": "line 17: `Number(row?.rule)` yields NaN whenever `block.rows.find(...)` matches no row, and that NaN is stored on the question as its `rule`; line 18: the fallback swallows the absence instead of treating a missing row as an error, and `line` and `ruleText` are taken from the question `q` rather than from the row, so the returned question can carry a NaN rule next to line/ruleText data that do not come from the same row."
+    },
+    {
+      "file": "src/blockasks.js",
+      "quote": "    if (q.ask === 'reading') return { ...base, ask: /** @type {'reading'} */ ('reading'), counted: true, ...(q.proposal == null ? {} : { reading: String(q.proposal) }), ...(Array.isArray(q.columns) ? { columns: q.columns } : {}), question: typeof q.question === 'string' ? q.question : readingQuestion(q.line, String(q.ruleText), String(q.proposal)) };\n    const words = plainWords(q.proposal);\n    return { ...base, ask: /** @type {'check'} */ ('check'), counted: false, reading: words, check: q.proposal, question: `Line ${q.line}, guardrail \"${q.ruleText}\": I propose ${words}.` };",
+      "why": "line 21: every `q.ask` value other than 'reading' falls through into the `check` branch, so any ask outside the two named kinds is silently relabelled as a check with `counted: false`; line 22: the check branch builds its words with `plainWords(q.proposal)` on a `q.proposal` that may be null or undefined, so it stringifies/plain-words an absent proposal and line 19 guards `reading` with `q.proposal == null` while the check branch does not, leaving `reading` and `check` disagreeing about the same missing proposal."
+    },
+    {
+      "file": "src/blockasks.js",
+      "quote": "  }).sort((a, b) => rank[a.ask] - rank[b.ask]);",
+      "why": "line 23: the final comparator has no tiebreak, so same-rank questions keep an arbitrary order, and when an `ask` value is not a key of `rank` (anything that fell through the `reading` test at line 21 with an unexpected label) `rank[a.ask]` is undefined and the subtraction gives NaN, which makes the sort order undefined for the whole list."
+    }
+  ]
+}
